limitations: Missing q^q/gamma^gamma factor in Lemma 3.3 — Counterevidence: For gamma=1 and 0<=q<=1 the omitted factor is at most one, so the printed coefficient still gives a weaker valid bound; this is the exponent used to start Theorems1.1/1.2.

Missing q^q/gamma^gamma factor in Lemma 3.3 — Counterevidence: Corrected coefficient is continuous and equals one at q=gamma, preserving the qualitative Proposition3.1 argument when c<1 and Lambda1>Lambda0.
Missing q^q/gamma^gamma factor in Lemma 3.3 — Counterevidence: The separate Neumann Lemma3.4 is not affected by this coefficient error.
Missing q^q/gamma^gamma factor in Lemma 3.3 — Counterevidence: Author arXiv2410.04769v2 pp19–20 has the same omission; no claim of a correction absent globally.

Missing q^q/gamma^gamma factor in Lemma 3.3 — Counterevidence: When gamma=1 and 0<=q<=1, q^q<=1, so the printed coefficient is already a weaker valid bound. Source page 26 starts Theorems 1.1/1.2 at gamma=1. The Neumann comparison is unaffected. Neither the principal theorem nor all downstream shape-optimization results are disproved.
The finding applies to the exact reviewed source version and inspected scope; uninspected publication versions are not adjudicated.

proposition.claim:
Write \[R_\eta^D(\lambda)
 =\sum_{k\geq1}(\lambda-\lambda_k^D(\Omega))_+^\eta,
 \qquad
 L^{\mathrm{sc}}_{\eta,d}
 =\frac{\Gamma(1+\eta)}
 {(4\pi)^{d/2}\Gamma(1+\eta+d/2)}.\] For \(\eta=0\), the paper uses the strict counting function \(\#\{k:\lambda_k^D(\Omega)<\lambda\}\); the counterexample below has strictly positive exponents and avoids that convention entirely. The Laplacians are the quadratic-form realizations on an open set.

Equation reference: eq:hyp, eq:false, eq:printedf. Set \(a=d/2\). Lemma 3.3 assumes \(d\geq2\), \(\gamma>0\), an open set \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d\) of finite volume, \(c>0\), and \(0<\Lambda\leq\infty\), with \[
 R_\gamma^D(\lambda)
 \leq cL^{\mathrm{sc}}_{\gamma,d}|\Omega|\lambda^{\gamma+a}
 \quad(0\leq\lambda\leq\Lambda).\] It claims, for every \(q=\gamma'\in[0,\gamma]\), that \[
 R_q^D(\lambda)
 \leq c f_\gamma^D(q)L^{\mathrm{sc}}_{q,d}|\Omega|\lambda^{q+a},
 \qquad
 0\leq\lambda\leq\frac{q+a}{\gamma+a}\Lambda,\] where the printed coefficient is \[
 f_\gamma^D(q)=
 \frac{(\gamma+a)^{\gamma+a}}{(q+a)^{q+a}}
 \frac{\Gamma(1+q+a)\Gamma(1+\gamma)}
 {\Gamma(1+\gamma+a)\Gamma(1+q)}.\] There is no restriction \(\gamma\geq1\) or \(c\geq1\) in the statement.

Recorded check: Missing q^q/gamma^gamma factor in Lemma 3.3

D: 2. Omega: (0,pi)^2; open, bounded, nonempty, convex, Lipschitz, finite area pi^2. Gamma: 1/4. Gamma prime: 1/8. Lambda: 5/2. C: 2/(pi*5^(1/4)) > 0. All energy premise: R_gamma(lambda) <= c L_gamma,2 pi^2 lambda^(gamma+1) for every 0<=lambda<=5/2, proved by the monotone normalized single-mode ratio. Test energy: 9/4=((1+1/8)/(1+1/4))*(5/2).
